project.name: payment-api
project.description:
Service-to-service contract for the payment / points domain (V9 §18 / §91).
Step 1 of two. Members: BillingBiz, the billing catalogue — the vocabulary a caller must speak to charge for anything.
Why it crosses a deployment unit. BillingBiz holds the biz_type values written to points_ledger.biz_type. Every charging call site has to name the thing it charges for, and those call sites live in six domains across three future deployment units: dinqor-agent (AgentConversationService, ImageGenerationTool, PublishPostTool), dinqor-platform-integration (CsdnMcpApplicationService, JuejinMcpApplicationService), dinqor-content-automation (EmailReminderScheduler, BlogAgentService) and dinqor-core-host (Img2ThreeService). The vocabulary is shared, so it cannot belong to the billing domain alone: after the split, four services would each need a copy or a dependency pointing into another service's internals.
Why this is a pure move and the port is not here yet. BillingBiz is a final class of String constants with a private constructor and no imports at all, so it moves without touching a single behaviour. BillingService — the other cross-domain type in this domain, imported by seven domains — is a concrete @Service over three MyBatis mappers, so it needs a port, not a move. That port is deliberately NOT in this commit: its chargeTokens(...) signature takes com.xander.lab.common.ModelUsage, which lives in libs/xander-model and carries a Jackson dependency (ModelUsage.fromJson), so the port forces a decision that has not been made yet — is a contract allowed to depend on a framework-free shared kernel, or must it own an equivalent DTO? See docs/migration/lib-extraction.md §3quinquies.5. Until that is answered this module holds the vocabulary only. The same shape as contracts/integration-api, which took the OSS pair and left the five concrete services behind.
Zero dependencies, and that is the point. A contract that drags in a framework cannot be depended on by every service, and V9 §19 is explicit that the WebFlux Gateway must stay free of spring-webmvc. Nothing here may gain a compile dependency without a deliberate decision; test scope is fine.
The package is com.xander.lab.payment.api rather than com.xander.lab.payment. "payment" is not a business domain (the domains are "billing" and "virtualpay"), but a bare first segment would still be classified as one by the cross-domain scanner and the contract would then be invisible in the metrics; the dotted entry "payment.api" is registered in SHARED_KERNEL for exactly that reason (see docs/migration/lib-extraction.md §6.1).
What is deliberately NOT here: ModelPrice / PointAccount / PointsLedger (persistence entities and the mapper projection targets), BillingProperties (configuration), and the price-calculation rules. Those are behaviour and stay in the billing domain.
